items.followUp: What are the two possible truth values of a proposition?

rubric.why: A truth value tells the truth status of a proposition.
rubric.description: Explains that a truth value indicates whether a proposition is true or false.

rubric.why: Propositions have one of two truth values.
rubric.description: Names both possible truth values: true and false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both values.

modelAnswer: The truth value of a proposition is its status as either true or false.

items.followUp: What is a denial-of-service attack, and what effect does it have?

rubric.description: Identifies or expands DoS as Denial of Service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attack as a denial-of-service attack.

rubric.why: The attack disrupts service by overwhelming a target with requests or traffic.
rubric.description: Explains that excessive requests or traffic make the targeted service unavailable to users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the disruption or unavailability caused by the attack.

modelAnswer: A DoS (Denial of Service) attack floods a computer system or network with excessive requests or traffic.
This can make the targeted service unavailable to its users.

items.followUp: Describe two warning signs of a phishing email.

rubric.why: Phishing websites often imitate legitimate websites to deceive visitors.
rubric.description: Identifies the website as fake or as an imitation of a legitimate site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the deceptive or lookalike website.

rubric.why: Phishing sites attempt to steal sensitive personal or financial information.
rubric.description: Mentions a request for sensitive details such as passwords or financial information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attempt to collect sensitive information.

modelAnswer: A phishing website may imitate a genuine website or use a fake login page to deceive visitors.
It may ask visitors for sensitive information, such as passwords, login credentials or financial details.
